Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.input:
n=19
centers=[(3,6,8),(4,13,4),(12,14,1),(14,3,2)]
# All gray arms, including arms of the uncolored cross at (10,8).
crosses=[(3,6),(4,13),(12,14),(14,3),(10,8)]
markers=set()
for r,c in crosses:
    markers.update([(r-1,c),(r+1,c),(r,c-1),(r,c+1)])
# Rays propagate from each colored center; its own gray arms are transparent,
# while arms belonging to any other cross stop that ray.
H=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]; V=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
for r,c,v in centers:
    for dc in (-1,1):
        j=c
        while 0<=j<n:
            if (r,j) in markers and abs(r-r)+abs(j-c)>1 and (r,j) not in {(r,c)}:
                # markers on this row are foreign unless they are own horizontal arms
                if (r,j) not in {(r,c-1),(r,c+1)}: break
            H[r][j]=v
            j+=dc
    for dr in (-1,1):
        i=r
        while 0<=i<n:
            if (i,c) in markers and (i,c) not in {(r-1,c),(r+1,c)}: break
            V[i][c]=v
            i+=dr
out=[[V[i][j] or H[i][j] for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
for r,c in markers: out[r][c]=3
assert len(out)==19 and all(len(row)==19 for row in out) and all(0<=x<=9 for row in out for x in row)
import json
print(json.dumps(out,separators=(',',':')))

# Key demo pattern: projection lines stop at cross gray arms rather than pass through other crosses.
n=19
centers=[(3,6,8),(4,13,4),(12,14,1),(14,3,2)]
crosses=[(3,6),(4,13),(12,14),(14,3),(10,8)]
arm_owner={}
for k,(r,c) in enumerate(crosses):
    for p in ((r-1,c),(r+1,c),(r,c-1),(r,c+1)): arm_owner[p]=k
H=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]; V=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
for k,(r,c,v) in enumerate(centers):
    for dr,dc,layer in [(0,-1,H),(0,1,H),(-1,0,V),(1,0,V)]:

        while 0<=i<n and 0<=j<n:
            # A ray stops before a different cross's center or any of its gray arms.
            if (i,j) in arm_owner and arm_owner[(i,j)]!=k: break

out=[[V[i][j] or H[i][j] for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
for p in arm_owner: out[p[0]][p[1]]=3
assert len(out)==19 and all(len(row)==19 for row in out)
import json
print(json.dumps(out,separators=(',',':')))

n=19
centers=[(3,6,8),(4,13,4),(12,14,1),(14,3,2),(10,8,0)]
markers={}
for k,(r,c,v) in enumerate(centers):

V=[[0]*n for _ in range(n)]
# Draw colored horizontal rays; own gray arms allow passage, foreign arms stop the ray.
for k,(r,c,v) in enumerate(centers):

    for dc in (-1,1):

            V[i][c]=v
            i+=dr

centers=[(3,6,8),(4,13,4),(12,14,1),(14,3,2)]
